title: Bent Creek: 7 mi 1000 ft elev. gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[Sign-up opens Sunday 5/3, 8:00 pm]**

Consider this a true **moderate-level** hike, somewhat longer and faster than my usual Friday morning jaunts. It's not an easy one, and not for beginners. We'll be covering 7 miles with at least a 2.5 mph pace.

Thanks to Todd for putting together this route, largely on Lower Sidehill Trail and South Ridge Rd. It's a pretty area deep into Bent Creek. The plan is for a "lollipop" with a short stem at the start and finish, and a big loop the rest of the way.

There's good footing throughout, with a combination of forest trails and gravel roads. If you're on the fence about poles, you probably won't need them here. Bring water and a snack if you're inclined. There'll be a little break somewhere around the middle.

**CARPOOLING TIME & PLACE**

There's very limited trailhead parking, so we'll carpool from the Asheville Outlets behind the Waffle House (directions below). Look for me and my silver Hyundai. Come early to allow for traffic. We'll depart by 9:00 AM

Here's the Waffle House location on Google Maps:
[https://goo.gl/maps/kjkQTmGQA7QNgbWLA](https://goo.gl/maps/kjkQTmGQA7QNgbWLA)

**From Exit 33 on I-26,**

* Head south a short distance on Brevard Rd. (Rt. 191) to the traffic light with Ingles on the right and Waffle House on the left.
* Turn Left into the Asheville Outlets.
* Drive just past the Waffle House and turn left onto the parking lot access road, NOT into the Waffle House lot.
* Take the first right. We'll park and meet in this area of the lot.

**ALSO IMPORTANT**
***Dogs.*** Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but U.S. Forest Service regulations require leashes. Wear sensible hiking boots. Bring some water. If you're on the fence about hiking poles, you probably don't need them for this one.

***Guests.*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they must join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike independently. Alternatively, contact me in advance to ask if it's okay to bring a +1 after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, we may be able to add your guest.

**COURTESY TO WAITLISTERS** (Please abide!)
Only sign up if you \*truly\* plan to come. And if you're on the borderline of dropping out for any reason, buck up and join us! I promise you'll be glad you did.

If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't ever be a "no-show" for any MeetUp events. Let your organizer know in advance.

If you're on the waiting list, keep checking the evening before. Despite what I wrote above, we usually have last-minute dropouts.

**WEATHER**
I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
If you have any questions, message me through MeetUp until 8:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (803) 767-3094.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-
**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group (AHG) event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can assure your safety nor eliminate all risks. Participants assume full responsibility for any damages or losses.

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Getting to Know the Birds of WNC
description:
Getting to Know the Birds of WNC
with Martha Rollefson 
Friday, May 8  |  10 – 12pm 
BRN – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
An introduction to the 60+ most common birds seen in Western North Carolina, grouped in fun and memorable ways: the birds we most love, the birds we “love to hate,” seen in the forests, seen around water, winter visitors, “knocking,” little but bold, those with different plumage for males and females, and so on.   Photos will be augmented with recordings from the Merlin app to identify birds by sound, and basic recommendations will be made for traditional field guides and attracting birds to your yard. 
Martha Rollefson has been a spare-time gardener for decades who got the “wildlife habitat” bug over 20 years ago. After leaving the corporate world she started working at Wild Birds Unlimited “to support her gardening habit,” and she joined the Western Carolina Botany Club to learn more about native plants. While feeding the birds and observing how gardening and wildlife interact, she has developed numerous techniques for saving time and money while reducing her carbon footprint. She lives next to the Etowah Valley Golf Resort with her husband David and mini-doxie, Eva.

title: Naturalist Walk and Talk – Native Orchids
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk – Native Orchids
with Shane Myers 
Friday, May 8  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN –  Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. This work included coordinating an Ohio- wide survey of dragonflies that culminated in a publication in 2024. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Snakes of the Blue Ridge
description:
Snakes of the Blue Ridge
with Patrick Brannon 
Friday, May 8  |  1 – 2:30pm 
BRN – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
Participants in this workshop will learn about the general biology of snakes, including the natural history and identification of many Southern Appalachian snake species. We will discuss the differences between venomous and non-venomous species, as well as dispelling many common misconceptions about snakes. 
Patrick Brannon is an independent naturalist and educator. He holds a M.S. in Biology from Appalachian State University, and has performed research on the ecology of salamanders and small mammals. For the past 22 years he was Outreach Coordinator at the WCU Highlands Biological Station, where he taught courses on amphibians and mammals as part of the UNC Institute for the Environment Program at HBS, in addition to many K-12 school programs and educator workshops.

title: Let's Take Swing Dance Lessons
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
Join us for Asheville Swing Night on **May 8th** for an evening of swing dancing, great music, and a fun beginner-friendly lesson. 💃🕺

We’re changing up the lesson format a bit this month based on feedback we received, and we think you’re going to love it.

Deb and Franklin will kick things off with the beginner fundamentals so everyone can learn the basic 6-count footwork and get comfortable with swing dancing. 🎶

Then, those who want to learn more can branch off with them to learn a few fun next-step moves, while the rest of us continue practicing in a relaxed group with help from our experienced dance assistants.

No partner needed. During both the lesson and social dance, most people rotate partners, making it a fun and easy way to meet people and get comfortable in the space.

(Most people come alone, by the way.)

**What dance are we learning?**
Intro Lindy Hop and East Coast Swing.

**How many people come?**
We typically have 55–65 people, and some months much more. It’s open to the public, not just this Meetup group.

**What should I wear?**
Wear shoes that are comfortable to dance in. Heels are not recommended. Leather-soled shoes or comfortable sneakers are best. Dressing up is optional - people wear everything from casual to vintage-inspired outfits.

## Logistics

📍 **Location:** Haw Creek Commons
Parking is onsite, or at Haw Creek Elementary if the lot is full. Just walk across the field to the venue.

🕖 **7:00 PM sharp** — Beginner swing dance lesson
(Please arrive on time, as the lesson builds progressively and is harder to join late if you're brand new.)

💃🕺 **8:00 PM – 10:30 PM** — Social dance with DJ

💵 **$10 admission** includes both the lesson and dance
Pay at the door (cash or Venmo)

🚪 Doors open at 6:45 PM

👥 Ages 12+

**More Info:**

https://www.facebook.com/events/792420760292163/

Website: [https://ashevilleswingnight.com/](https://ashevilleswingnight.com/)

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Pressed Flower Art Workshop
description:
Pressed Flower Art Workshop
with Susan McChesney 
Saturday, May 9  |  10 – 1pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Experience the art of Oshibana, the Japanese tradition of making art with pressed plant materials. Learn a technique of pressing, unpressing, storing, collaging and sealing flower petals to create a work of art. All materials and a comprehensive resource sheet provided. Make a collage that will be sealed, matted and sleeved in the workshop. 
Susan McChesney is a pressed flower artist who uses pressed petals like strokes of paint in landscape collages. A longtime educator, the Oshibana technique she practices, creating art with pressed plant materials, is adaptable to a successful workshop experience. As a practicing artist, her work is shown at various venues in Western NC.

title: World Bonsai Day
location: Bonsai Exhibition Garden
description:
World Bonsai Day
May 9, 2026
11:00 a.m. – 6:00 p.m.
  
World Bonsai Day weekend May 9 marks the official opening of the Arboretum’s internationally acclaimed Bonsai Exhibition Garden, with trees filling the benches for the first time since fall! 
Arthur Joura, Bonsai Curator at The North Carolina Arboretum, will present a free live bonsai demonstration in the Bonsai Exhibit Garden at 1 p.m. 
To mark the occasion, the Blue Ridge Bonsai Society will be onsite with educational displays and to answer questions from visitors. 
The North Carolina Arboretum is a World Bonsai Friendship Federation Cooperation Center, one of only eight so designated bonsai gardens across the world which all celebrate World Bonsai Day each year by presenting bonsai experiences to the public. 
The World Bonsai Day celebration is included with the Arboretum’s regular parking fee. 
This event is part of Spring Into the Arb! Celebrate the return of spring with a series of events and happenings throughout March, April, May and June! Spring is a time of renewal and emergence, and The North Carolina Arboretum is excited to welcome this season with plant shows, nature programs, education, music, art and more!

title: River Systems Field Class
description:
River Systems Field Class
with Anton DuMars 
Saturday, May 9  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
For the River Systems Field Experience, we will observe processes and indicators along the Davidson River, a Blue Ridge tributary of the French Broad catchment basin. We consider channel hierarchy (first order, second order, etc.). Our stops include observation and discussions of flow and flood indicators and river forms, such as cut banks, point bars, and flood channels. We observe sediment texture, sediment load, and consider sediment source. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat.

title: Choose a 5 KM or 10 KM City Walk in Greenville SC
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
There is a large parking garage just behind the Westin Hotel, 120 South Main St., Greenville.

There is also a free parking lot on the roof of the building at the corner of W North St. and Richardson St. Walk from the south side of the parking lot to Main St. Turn right on Main and go 3 blocks to Joel's Java Coffee Shop (next to the Westin Hotel).

We'll gather and register at Joel's Java Coffee Shop at 12:30 p.m. It is National Butterscotch Brownie Day. Perhaps Joel's will have some for purchase. You'll surely want to try one of their treats at any rate.

We are doing this walk with the Asheville Amblers, AARP, Stryder, and perhaps others. The walk is free, although the Amblers do accept donations ($4 suggested donation). Step-off is at 1:00.

Choose between a 5 KM guided walk and a 10 KM guided walk. Both walks have some moderate hills and stair climbing and are mostly on pavement.

Both walks include a beautiful stroll through Falls Park with spectacular falls and along the Reedy River. You will take in part of the Swamp Rabbit Trail. The walk also takes you down both sides of Main Street, where you'll try to find the little brass mice hidden there. The 10 KM walk also includes a fine neighborhood, a large park with shaded and open trails, the zoo, and more of the Swamp Rabbit Trail.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Tennis shoes will be fine. Walking sticks are not needed by most. Bring a protein snack and plenty of water. Take care of restroom needs before the walk; the 10 KM walk passes restrooms at the zoo. Strollers and wheelchairs are not recommended.

Greenville is a wonderful, family-friendly city. Many will want to come early for lunch at one of the many wonderful restaurants along Main Street. Some may want to explore more after the walk and perhaps stay for supper. Plan to enjoy your visit.

title: Spring Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum
description:
Spring Wildflowers of the NC Arboretum
with Lauren Lampley 
Saturday, May 9  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
Interested in learning how to identify wildflowers? Join Lauren on this walk around the Arboretum property where we will go over different ways of identifying plants and different families of flowers. Some flowers are very difficult to identify to species and some are relatively easy so we will talk about how to get as close as possible with tools we can easily carry into the field. We will be using Newcomb’s guide to key out some of the less common flowers but will focus on learning how to look closely at flowers in order to identify them. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

Slow down and be with yourself through art making. A rich morning that feeds your spirit, rests your body, quiets your mind and helps you remember who you are!

title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky.

description:

Please read the entire description. There is a choice.

We'll start at the parking lot at Fresh Market, Hendersonville Rd., take the spur trail, which is a little tricky, to MST, and head west to the bridge at Dingle Creek, which is our turn around. The trail has been immaculately restored after Helene. Also, sections that were heavily forested with a dense upper canopy are now amazingly opened to the sky.

This is not a difficult hike. It's a smooth trail with gradual elevation. We'll hike at a slow pace, between 2.0 and 2.5 mph. Out and back is about 5.5 miles. Expect to spend 2.5 to 3.0 hours hiking on the trail.

**For those wanting a longer hike Craig-like hike**, you can take off after Dingle Creek and hike down to the new bridge over I-26. There and back to Fresh Market is approx. 7. 5 miles. The MST at the new bridge is currently closed--construction/landscaping.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura
description:
Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura
Tuesday, May 12  |  5:30 – 7pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Join Bonsai Curator Arthur Joura on this entertaining and informative after-hours tour of the garden at its peak in spring, a fitting showcase for the specimens and the miniature landscapes. As Joura says, “The two things are one: The garden is designed to elevate the experience of bonsai, and the bonsai never look better than when they’re on display in the garden.” 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Arthur Joura has been the bonsai curator at the Arboretum since 1992 and oversaw the design and development of the Arboretum’s Bonsai Exhibition Garden. Joura augmented early training in fine art and studied bonsai with some of the leading bonsai authorities in the United States and in Japan. His greatest teachers are trees, however. His love of hiking and photographing trees in nature has shaped the Arboretum’s collection and firmly rooted it in a regional identify — one that elevates naturalism in art and the use of traditional bonsai species alongside species native to the Southern Appalachian mountains — creating in the process one of the most acclaimed public collections of bonsai in the country..

title: Scenic AVL #7: Scott Mountain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
There is very limited parking at the [trailhead](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fETct2fiMiLz1HEG8). Please plan to meet at Lake Hills Church parking lot at 10 minutes before the start to condense cars.
Lake Hills Church Parking Lot is pictured above.
- [https://maps.app.goo.gl/X1TctrhYv3gihmh66](https://maps.app.goo.gl/X1TctrhYv3gihmh66)
*Call the hike leader at 828-290-0886 if you cannot find us. Do not text.

**Rating**: Moderate
**Elevation**: 800
**Distance**: 5 miles
**Surface**: Trail
**Pace**: 3 mph
**Dogs**: on leash.
**Gear**: Long pants recommended, bug spray, water. The ticks are bad on this trail. Bring your bug spray !
**Features**: wooded trail, interesting plants and fungi. Bears are shy, but we may see them, also deer and squirrels. 3 miles uphill, 2.25 down.
**All Trails Route**:
[Scott Mountain Loop on AllTrails](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/scott-mountain-loop-4217403?p=-1&sh=ifwm3x)

[Scenic Asheville Series](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk): there are 9 hikes in the series, plus a few wild cards. Hike 9 of them and receive an [attractive](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) badge for your backpack. If you have a badge , you can always come on
a hike , even if you are on the waiting list .
RSVP and On-Time Start:

- If you decide you cannot come, please change your RSVP
*If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers can have sufficient notice.
- There are generally 1 or 2 no-shows on my hikes, so we don't wait for people to arrive. If you are late, you'll be left behind.
*Please note that there is never cell coverage at the start of the hike, so please change your RSVP as soon as you know you can't make it.
- Notes and comments are genuinely appreciated.

**Guests**: Make sure your guests are fit enough to complete the hike. if someone is a guest, their hike will not count toward a badge because there will not be a record of their name .

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

title: AI Hacks and Hops - From Chatbot to Co-Worker: AI for Business
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**From Chatbot to Co-Worker: A Business Guide to AI That Actually Works**
**Speaker:** [Julio Barros](https://www.linkedin.com/in/juliobarros/)

**Description:** Most business owners use AI the way people used the internet in 1996, they check the weather. They type questions into ChatGPT, read the answer, and close the tab. Meanwhile, a quiet revolution is underway: small teams are using AI agents to run real business operations, following up with leads, generating reports, managing content pipelines, and handling customer support autonomously.
The gap between "asking AI questions" and "giving AI a job" is the biggest competitive window most of us will see in our careers. But closing that gap wrong is worse than not closing it at all.
This session walks you through the progression from chatbot to co-worker with live demonstrations, then gives you a practical framework for identifying where to start in your own business - and what order to do it in so you don't automate the wrong thing first.

**General Event Info**
AI Hacks and Hops is a monthly event tailored for non-technical professionals, entrepreneurs, marketers, engineers, or anyone who wants to explore and discuss how to use AI.

Each gathering will feature presentations, stimulating group discussions, and a relaxed atmosphere for enjoying your favorite brews while delving into the world of AI. Topics will range from AI integration in business processes, marketing, content creation, software, ethical considerations, human-AI collaboration strategies, to the latest advancements in AI technology. The informal setting encourages open dialogue, idea exchange, and fosters a collaborative spirit.

title: Wednesday night Bent Creek
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
RSVP's don't open until 6PM Sunday night.
Weather: will know more by Monday and will let everyone know the details then.
I did this hike series for many years before 2022, but I did it as a high-speed hike, and I am now doing it as a moderate speed hike. This is a numbers limited event and I expect people who sign-up to show up. Late cancellations, and those that don't show up are bumping other interested hikers, and they will not be allowed on future hikes.
If all goes well, I will try to post a hike most weeks, and for days Tue or Wed, distance, and start location, like switching between Hard Times trail-head and Bent Creek River Park, may change.
The current route is about 5.5 miles.
Please folks, this is intended as a moderate paced hike, and we'd like all attendees to keep up with the hike leader(s). This hike is intended as a workout hike for people to get in condition to do weekend hikes.
Moderate paced means 22-24 min miles, or 2 ½ mph.
As such, we do not take breaks, take in views, or snap photos along the way. Please make sure you're able to keep up with the group. This hike has always served as a good chance to get exercise during the week, meet new people, and create interest for weekend enjoyment hikes. It's a great introduction to the AHG family.
No need to RSVP "No" or "not attending" unless changing from a "Yes."
Please read the full description before RSVPing, and only sign up if you are sure you can go. Thanks in advance for keeping your RSVP up-to-date and not being a last-minute cancellation or no-show. This is an ongoing issue with Meetups and often keeps people on waitlists from being able to attend our hikes.
Hard Times Trailhead near Lake Powhatan Rec Area
Follow signs off of Brevard Rd (Rt 191) to Lake Powhatan Rec Area. The road is Bent Creek Ranch Rd. to Wesley Branch Rd. Follow signs to Lake Powhatan until you come to Hard Times Trailhead on your left, 2.5 miles. It is very clearly marked. Parking is very limited at the trailhead but there’s a paved pull-off just before the Hard Times trailhead and more parking just beyond at the Ledford Branch trailhead. We will access Bent Creek forest by way of Hard Times Trail and do some combination of loop and out and back.
Arrive at the trailhead BY 6:00. Because it is a weeknight hike, we are unable to wait for latecomers, fighting daylight.
\*\*\*If you are running behind, please post a comment on this Meetup page by 5:45 pm. There is no cell service at the parking lot, so if we don't have any advance notice of you running late by 5:45, we can't get any notifications at the trailhead and we will not wait for you.
We start the hike at 6:00, rarely do we get much later than that.
• Wear closed-toed footwear appropriate for hiking. The trail will consist of dirt, rocks, roots, mud and mulch.
• Bring plenty of water.
• Bring rain gear if a chance of rain is in the forecast.
Headlamps suggested
• Dogs on leashes the whole time are welcome. This is an active mountain bike area and it can get messy with dogs running loose among hikers and mountain bikers.
Please make sure to keep your RSVP up-to-date. You don't want to be "that person" who cancels last minute or no-shows and keeps someone from joining in if there's a waitlist. Thanks for your consideration - it is appreciated!
Feel free to post questions not covered in this description in the comments section.
Thanks - we'll see you on the trail!

title: NC Arboretum Blue Ghost Firefly Night Hike
description:
NC Arboretum Blue Ghost Firefly Night Hike
with Shane Myers and Asheville Wellness Tours 
Wednesday, May 13  |  7:30 – 10:30 pm 
(rain date is Thursday, May 14) 
REGISTER HERE 
Immerse yourself in the magic of twilight and experience the wonders of nighttime in the Blue Ridge Mountains. From sunset and starry skies to fireflies, we’ll marvel at Mother Nature’s light shows as we explore the forest, hoping to encounter the elusive Blue Ghost Firefly species! Out of the 26 species of firefly we have in western North Carolina, the Blue Ghost (Phausis reticulata) might be the most magical. With a very limited range, and a distinctive meandering flight, we have a lot to learn from observing these nocturnal jewels. Tonight we’ll talk about what makes a firefly light up, what their lives are like, and how we can make sure they are around for generations to come. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio. He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum. 
This event is a collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours and they are handling all of the registration through their system. They have graciously included our Membership Discount promo code in their system so if you are an Arboretum member don’t forget to input your code to get your 10% off. title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Friday, May 15th
Evening Dance Wave 7:00 pm \- 9:00 pm \| Warmup 7pm \| Opening Circle 7:30pm
Guest DJ Karen Funshine \| Facilitator Ted Riskin

Intention: Embrace You-Ness
“You-Ness” is the essence of you, a completely unique blend of your genetic & astrological blueprint, your life experiences, your spirit, talents, & desires. Within you lives a full spectrum of personalities, from the wounded child to the wise sage, from the artist to the scientist and so many varied expressions in between. This dance is an invitation to step fully into that multi-dimensional being and welcome all parts of yourself, raw, real, and FREE. Drop the mask of your "usual self" and allow what’s been hidden or suppressed to breathe, move, be seen and felt, whether it be the elegant or the profane, the tender or the fierce, the serious or the sensual, the timid or the wild one. There is no bad or wrong part of you. It's all perfect, whole & complete. Together, we celebrate radical self-acceptance rather than comparison and rediscover the freedom of being wholly, unapologetically you. In the words of the great Dr. Seuss, "Today you are You, that is truer than true. There is no one alive who is Youer than You". So, let's dive in and get curious about which parts of us show up when we invite them into our dance with loving, open arms, minds, & hearts.

About the DJ
Karen Funshine (Karen Smith) has been dancing since age 3, with movement as her lifelong ally. A veteran raver & EDM enthusiast, she was delighted to discover 5Rhythms and ecstatic dance 10 years ago in Austin - a sober and judgment-free space to get wild & free. She’s since facilitated many women’s conscious dance circles and a vibrant live-instrument dance - weaving music and somatic movement to alchemize emotion, open the heart, and awaken joy. Recently relocated to Asheville, Karen is honored to share her passion and playfulness with her beautiful new community through the universal language of music and dance.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

When we integrate with intention, we move through change with greater clarity, resilience, and compassion for ourselves and others.

We are delighted to welcome Becca Marshall as our circle holder. Becca is an Integrative Psychotherapist, Aligned Living Coach, Psychedelic Integration Guide, and founder of [ActivXchange](https://www.activxchange.com/) — Her work supports people navigating significant life transitions, entering adulthood, stepping into leadership, moving through healing and transformation, with grounded presence and genuine care.

This circle is open to anyone curious, those actively preparing for or integrating an experience, and those who have been walking this path for years. Our intention is simple: to foster connection, shared wisdom, and mutual support within our growing community here in Asheville. All are welcome.

A suggested donation of $10 helps cover venue costs and support future PSA offerings. No one will ever be turned away for lack of funds.

We look forward to being in circle with you. 💫

title: Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 2.0
description:
Friendly People in Asheville
It’s spring, y’all, so it’s time for **Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 2.0**. 🎉

Same fun hunt, all new clues. Whether you joined our hunt last fall or are brand new to the game, come out and give it a try! This is a fun way to explore Asheville and make new friends.

Here’s how it works:

We will gather at the S&W Market at 56 Patton Avenue at 2:30pm. We’ll hang out upstairs — at Periscope — and get snacks and drinks, etc. If you’re a little late, no worries.

We will break up into teams and go over the rules at 3:15pm. Teams will have 10-15 minutes to review the clues, and the hunt will begin at 3:30pm.

Teams will have an hour to hunt for 40 clues scattered across downtown and take a selfie with each clue. \*Bonus points for taking a selfie with the clue and a willing stranger. More willing strangers = more points.\*

The hunt ends at 4:30pm back at Periscope in the S&W.

It will take 20-30 minutes to review all the teams’ answers and determine the winner.
The prize will be the glory of winning! 🏆
That said, this hunt’s 40th question is a diabolical bonus question with only one correct answer. Get it right, and I’ll buy you (and everyone on your team) a drink.

**What to bring:**

* Walking or running shoes (the hunt spans from South Slope to the north end of downtown)
* Your phone for taking pics
* A pencil or pen to mark off clues as you find them
* Your competitive spirit!

**Parking:**
Parking is available nearby at the Rankin (68 Rankin Ave) and Wall Street (45 Wall Street) parking decks, as well as at the Coxe Ave Garage (52 Coxe Ave). Metered street parking is also available around the corner on Church Street.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
Participants are responsible for their safety. If you sign up or participate in this event, you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event.

Looking forward to seeing y’all there!

title: Change of Seasons: Spring Into Ikebana
description:

May 16 – 17, 2026
9:00 a.m. – 5:00 p.m.
  
The Ikebana International Asheville Chapter will present an exhibition of ikebana, the disciplined Japanese art of floral arrangement. Through intentional use of line, color, space, contrast, and texture, these works transform plant materials into expressive designs that reflect harmony between humanity and nature, creating beauty and a sense of calm. 
  
This event is part of Spring Into the Arb! Celebrate the return of spring with a series of events and happenings throughout March, April, May and June! Spring is a time of renewal and emergence, and The North Carolina Arboretum is excited to welcome this season with plant shows, nature programs, education, music, art and more!

title: Gardens of Haywood Community College + 3 Laps of the Bobcat Trail
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Three laps on the Bobcat Trail amounts to 3.1 miles. Bobcat consists of both natural and paved surfaces. There is a little elevation change on the route, but nothing too strenuous.

We will stop to look at a different garden on each counterclockwise lap. The first lap we will stop at the Bird and Butterfly Garden. The second lap we will stop at the Dahlia Garden. The third lap we will stop at the Rhododendron Garden. All three should be in beautiful bloom. Bring your camera!

As you enter the campus from Jones Cove Road, go to the first parking lot on the left. We will gather there and then head out.

Be sure to dress for the weather. Consider sunscreen and a hat. I'm going to wear tennis shoes, unless it has rained a lot recently (in which case, I will wear light hiking boots). I plan to bring my walking sticks.

As always, you are urged to bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should not have much problem. There are no bathrooms available that afternoon, so take care of such needs before you arrive.

title: Burton St Community Association Monthly Meeting
Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

title: Introduction to Permaculture & Permaculture Plants of Interest
description:
Introduction to Permaculture & Permaculture Plants of Interest
with Jennifer Verprauskus 
Thursday, May 21  |  10 – 12pm 
BREG – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
Learn how to bridge the gap between traditional landscape practices and self-sustaining systems taught in Permaculture. Landscape Architect and Permaculture Design Certificate Holder Jennifer Verprauskus covers basic design principles together with permaculture design concepts. Maximizing natural, beneficial relationships in the ecosystem while minimizing waste and energy use makes for an ideal landscape that nurtures itself and fits seamlessly into the natural environment. 
This class focuses on choosing the best plants for a site, with an emphasis on incorporating edible and native plants into the landscape planting design. Students will be introduced to a myriad of permaculture plants and learn the attractive and beneficial qualities they offer, including historical uses and wildlife benefits to structure and color — all considerations in creating a successful and sustainable landscape. 
Jennifer Verprauskus is a North Carolina Licensed Landscape Architect and a Permaculture Design Certificate Holder. She studied Landscape Architecture at the University of Massachusetts & Cal Poly. Since graduating, she has traveled the world to help people grow trees and their own food. She is the founder of both UpBeet Landscapes and BareRoot Designs, PLLC.

title: Third Thursday: Small Business Appreciation Night featuring Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts of Holler Choir
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Celebrate Small Business Month at May’s Third Thursday with a special Small Business Appreciation Night, presented by Bank of America, at the Asheville Art Museum. In conjunction with the exhibition In a New Light: American Impressionism 1870–1940, Works from the Bank of America Collection, enjoy an afternoon and evening of community connection featuring live music, hands‑on creativity, and more. 
As the evening unfolds, Asheville-based, nationally recognized musicians Jackson Grimm and Clint Roberts will perform in the Museum’s Windgate Foundation Atrium from 6–8 pm. Grimm and Roberts—also members of the popular band Holler Choir—blend old-time and swing band traditions with indie rock, creating a sound that’s both unique and deeply satisfying. 
Settle in and enjoy the music, grab a drink from the Perspective Café pop‑up bar, then stroll the galleries and experience your favorite artworks after hours. Don’t forget to stop by the Studio to silkscreen your own poster to take home—a creative keepsake from a night celebrating art, music, small businesses, and our vibrant local community. 
ABOUT THE MUSICIANS

Jackson Grimm is an accomplished and respected band leader, multi-instrumentalist and teacher in the Western North Carolina music community. His songs marry folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. In a region with a strong music culture, it is no surprise that Grimm’s songwriting is representative of his musical birthplace: Asheville. 
Grimm won the 2025 LEAF Songwriting competition and has been a 2 year finalist for the Songwriter Serenade. He has shared the stage with and opened up for acts such as Molly Tuttle, Sierra Ferrell, Shadowgrass, the Wilder Flower, Arlo Guthrie, Tim Grimm, Ben Bedford, Ordinary Elephant, Nathan Evans Fox, and more.” 
Clint Roberts was raised in the Appalachian mountains of Western North Carolina and crafts songs that bridge the gap between the region’s deep-rooted folk traditions and the contemporary Americana heard on national airwaves. After dedicating a decade to his solo singer-songwriter career beginning in his early twenties, Clint founded the collective-driven string band Holler Choir in Asheville in 2021. 
Since then, Holler Choir has toured extensively across the United States and expanded its creative reach by becoming the backing band for a second project, the Susto String Band, formed in collaboration with the band Susto. In 2024, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Jackson Grimm joined both Holler Choir and the Susto String Band and now co-leads the project alongside Clint.

That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:
Walking Meditation & Qigong
with Jenne Sluder 
Friday, May 22  |  9 – 10am

Enjoy a slow, mindful walking meditation through the gardens, practicing breath awareness and sensory attention to touch the deep peace and simple wonders of quiet time in nature. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

title: The Arb in Focus: 40 Views for 40 Years
location: Baker Exhibit Center
description:
The Arb in Focus: 40 Views for 40 Years
May 23 – September 12, 2026
Baker Exhibit Hall

See the Arboretum from the viewpoint of those most familiar with it! 
The Arb in Focus: 40 Views for 40 Years is a photography project celebrating the Arboretum’s 40th anniversary. For the occasion, 40 people connected to the Arboretum, either as staff, members, or volunteers have taken ‘point and shoot’ digital cameras onto the grounds to photograph what matters most to them, using small pocket digital cameras. 
The collected photographs represent hundreds of moments on the grounds – on the trails, in the formal gardens and ‘behind the scenes.’ Though the beauty of the gardens is certainly part of the experience, viewers of The Arb in Focus can expect more than plants, trees, and trails, as participating photographers capture candid moments and sights that convey what it looks like to spend a day at the Arboretum. 
After the completion of The Arb in Focus, the cameras will be used for the Education department’s Discovery summer camps. 
The Arb in Focus is sponsored by community partner Mosaic Realty.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: May 23rd Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**[Click HERE to register!](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-23rd-community-cuddles)**

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**
1\. Clothes stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\.
4\. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with\.
5\. Speak up if you have a question\, concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. All emotions are welcome\- we love vulnerability\.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.
* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Holiday Weekend Sunday Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
What better way to spend the Sunday afternoon before Memorial Day than by walking with a meetup group?

Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 clockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

title: Code with Asheville Monthly Meeting
description:
Asheville Tech Events
Are you curious or even passionate about using advocacy, technology and sensible design to create more equitable social and civic structures in Western North Carolina?

Whether you call yourself an organizer, a technologist, a designer, planner, concerned resident, all of the above or something else entirely, we want to be in relationship and build community together with you.
Check out a list of our current projects: [https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects](https://github.com/CodeForAsheville/projects)

What to expect:
Since project work takes place asynchronously—individually and in smaller squads—the goals of our monthly gatherings are to:

* build relationships and learn about each other's skills, interests and goals,
* learn what we are doing across the organization (project updates),
* provide opportunities to get involved with and/or initiate projects, and
* shape where we are going as an organization, co-creating the culture and course of our work together.

In this meeting, we will:

* gather virtually using Google Meet for group video chat,
* do brief introductions, with a prompt,
* share updates about the projects that we're working on, highlighting deliverables for the next month and areas where additional resources would be useful, and
* discuss proposals and new opportunities to engage with local government and community organizations.

It isn't all glamorous, but the stakes are low for showing up and we'd be delighted to join together with you in this work.

title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.
